Senses.PreferredTarget: look at the word or saying
Senses.Explanation: Literally, ‘look at the talk’: look at the word, saying, question, or conversational thread singled out in a record. The compound most often occurs in ‘look at the saying's head’ (看話頭), and the local wording—not an imported technical label—determines whether English says word, saying, question, or thread. The records include a monk seeking written direction because the saying he was looking at had not opened to him. They also preserve criticism: Mingben reports people calling looking at a saying ‘doing work’ and rejects their appeal to direct transmission; Yuancheng says an old hunter neither did work nor looked at a saying before answering that there was ‘no place to set a hand,’ and contrasts this with looking left and right at one's own selected saying. Another record demands, ‘if you recognize it and can say it, come out and say it—what does the end of the talk say?’ Thus the Zen deviation is an ordinary act of looking directed at actual words in recorded exchanges and itself subjected to criticism in the record.
Senses.Note: No separate sense is created for different possible English renderings of “talk” (話) in context; they are readings of the same act and object family. Exact “look at the talk” (看話) also occurs across word boundaries in ordinary prose, so only lexically coherent deployments are curated.

Occurrences.Kwic: 說著箇看話頭做工夫。遽引信心銘，謂執之失度，必入邪路。剛謂直指單傳，無如是事。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Mingben reports and criticizes calling looking at a saying ‘doing work’; the entry does not adopt that category.

Occurrences.Kwic: 因看話頭處未通，出紙求指示
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A monk requests written direction because the saying he is looking at remains unresolved.

Occurrences.Kwic: 初不做工夫、亦不看話頭，一聞恁麼舉便云無下手處
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 湛然圓澄禪師語錄. Full six-rung exact-turn review identifies Zhanran Yuancheng as the exact headword-bearing speaker, author, or grammatical actor for this occurrence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 識得道得出來道看話端道什麼
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), in Yunmen Wenyan's record. Yunmen Wenyan is the exact speaker challenging the assembly about 看話.
